nse:106830108.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106830108.answer: In June 2025, management guided for 8% to 10% annual revenue growth and prudent PBT margins around 15%. In November 2025, management expected FY26 revenue around ₹12,500 crore and average margins of 15%+. Q2 FY27 revenue dropped 16.5% YoY to ₹2,446.1 crore and EBITDA margin fell to 8.1%, missing these expected growth and margin targets.

evidence.quote: As the Director of Finance has brought out, we expect the revenue growth of anywhere between 8% to 10% and our PBT margins we expect around 15%
We anticipate that this year, we will have revenue of approximately INR 12,500 crores or so
But on an average, we can anticipate around 15% plus margins

nse:106829089.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106829089.answer: Management did not give specific numerical guidance for Q2 FY27 revenue or margins. In the Q1 FY27 call (August 2026), management stated they do not provide guidance. However, for Bluetile, they noted user acquisition investments defer margins upfront, leading to an 11% EBITDA margin in Q1, but providing future flexibility to adjust EBITDA.

evidence.quote: At Nazara level, do we want to give any guidance in terms of revenue, EBITDA, or margin? Nitish Mittersain: Not at this point of time
It's just that the margins are deferred because all the user acquisition cost is being absorbed upfront. Eventually, this will, of course, normalize into much higher EBITDA margins being reported
So, the EBITDA margins in Q1 last year was 17.6%, now it is around 11%

nse:106823393.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106823393.answer: In July 2026 (Q1 FY27 call), management indicated margin improvements could continue near-term. In October 2026 (Q2 FY27 call), CFO Akshant Goyal stated food delivery margins are expected to remain flattish over the next 1–2 years while reinvesting in growth, with quick commerce NOV growth picking up from Q3. Q2 FY27 actual revenue (+77.6% YoY) and EBITDA margin (3.1%) align with this strategy.

evidence.quote: It's hard to project or comment on margin trajectory every quarter but broadly, over the next 1 or 2 years, we expect the margins to remain flattish
Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards

Is it safe to say that as long as growth in the business continues as per your expectations, which you said should be robust, there are no near-term pressures on margins that we should anticipate and directionally, margin should continue to improve? Is that like a fair conclusion? Akshant Goyal: At this point, we can say that

nse:106818661.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106818661.answer: In August 2026, management anticipated their Q2 FY27 large deal would be accretive to revenue and margins from Q2 onwards. In October 2026, Q2 EBIT margin was reported at 15%, down 100 bps QoQ and 130 bps YoY, while reported PAT margin dropped to 7.5% due to one-time Nagarro acquisition expenses.

evidence.quote: And yes, it will be accretive - revenue & margin from Q2 onwards
EBIT margins for Q2 FY27 came in at 15%, 130 basis points declined year-on-year
Reported profit after tax for the quarter was Rs. 3,515.1 million, a margin of 7.5%, with year-on-year decline of 25.4%

nse:106810133.question: What has management said about debt, leverage and its credit profile?
nse:106810133.answer: In Q4 FY26 (Apr 2026), management explained leverage is split between core infra (net external debt ~$5B, regulatory asset base ~$4B, 3.5x-4.5x leverage range) and metals/mining ($2B debt vs $6B assets, conservative profile). Total leverage stood at 3.9x and is expected to stay flat or decline. Incremental debt for incubating businesses was ~INR 36,000 crores in Q3 FY26.

evidence.quote: we keep a low or very conservative leverage profile on the metal, materials and mining side, given the volatilities we face in those businesses. And we keep the normal core infra profile on the core infra side.
don't expect the numbers next year to be materially different from this, including our capex plan of about $4.5 billion. So the 3.9x is likely to remain either flat or slightly down
Yes, we will actually provide a lot more detail, but just basically, our incremental total external debt now is roughly around over INR36,000 crores (that is allocated to our incubating businesses)

nse:106805308.question: What has management said on recent calls about leadership, succession or this role?
nse:106805308.answer: In October 2026 (Q2 FY27), Sashidhar Jagdishan announced the end of his tenure, welcoming Anup Bagchi as the new leader, while Bagchi expressed gratitude for his appointment as MD & CEO. Jagdishan also announced Deputy MD Kaizad Bharucha's early retirement by December 2026. In July 2026 (Q1 FY27), management welcomed Rajiv Kumar as the bank's new Chairman.

evidence.quote: I'll also leave behind in the hands of an able team spread across various levels in the organization throughout the country, led by a new and an able leader, and I welcome Anup at this juncture heartily to the institution as well
I'm really grateful to the Board for the trust placed in me as MD and CEO
I think the world would have just got another notification to the exchanges that our dear colleague, Kaizad, has requested for an early retirement by end of December

nse:106830187.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106830187.answer: In the Q4 FY26 call (April 2026), management declined to give explicit numerical forward guidance for revenue or margins due to macro/geopolitical uncertainties. However, they expressed optimism for revenue, targeting >10% volume growth and healthy ASPs, while anticipating temporary margin pressures from commodities/energy. The reported Q2 FY27 results show 26.0% revenue growth but lower margins (EBITDA margin 8.9% vs 12.0%).

evidence.quote: So it's always difficult to give out a guidance on margins
The broad expectation, which our Chairman also conveyed, is growth of over 10% this year as compared to the last year
So yes, there is some pressure, but we are taking it as part of regular business

nse:106816143.question: What has management said on recent calls about leadership, succession or this role?
nse:106816143.answer: In the Q1 FY27 call (August 2026), management announced the appointment of Raymond Stauffer as Nazara's new CEO, effective September 1, 2026. Managing Director Nitish Mittersain stated that Stauffer will manage day-to-day group operations, while Mittersain focuses on long-term strategy, portfolio direction, M&A, key relationships, and emerging technologies.

evidence.quote: Yesterday, we announced our Q1 Results, the appointment of Raymond Stauffer as our new CEO, effective September 1 2026, subject to relevant regulatory approvals, and an acceleration of the previously announced Bluetile and BestPlay transaction to acquire 100% ownership for a fixed all-cash consideration of $303 million
As Founder and Managing Director, I will continue to shape Nazara's long-term strategy, portfolio direction, and key relationships, working closely with Raymond and the Board
The CEO, Raymond, will be completely responsible for the day-to-day operations of the entire group and will be fully empowered to execute appropriately

nse:106799352.question: Has management discussed this case or its possible financial impact on its calls?
nse:106799352.answer: Management did not discuss this on its last two calls.

nse:106829216.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106829216.answer: In Q1 FY27, management stated EBITDA margins (8% in Q1) would ramp up further in subsequent quarters towards a near-term 15–20% target, and aimed for revenue growth higher than 28%. Q2 FY27 results match this expectation, with revenue growth accelerating to 28.5% YoY (₹2,648 crore) and EBITDA margin expanding to 10.2%.

evidence.quote: The thing is that we probably announced 8% of EBITDA margin this quarter. There is going to be a ramp up from here. It has to grow forward
So we're seeing that growth pretty much across the board and we think, having achieved this number, we should aim for even higher
And EBITDA, we will maintain about two and a half to three years from now, that we should be able to get to those sorts of EBITDA margins

nse:106827323.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106827323.answer: In the Q4 FY26 call, management declined to provide specific numerical guidance on revenue or margins due to dynamic market conditions. They noted cost headwinds from commodities and energy, while expressing confidence in returning to a healthy margin trajectory and targeting over 10% volume growth for FY27 once war-related pressures ease.

evidence.quote: It will be difficult to put a number. But yes, in such a situation some cost headwinds do come and it's part of business
So it's always difficult to give out a guidance on margins
The broad expectation, which our Chairman also conveyed, is growth of over 10% this year as compared to the last year

nse:106826436.question: What had management said on recent calls about revenue and margins for this period, and does this result match it?
nse:106826436.answer: In the Q1 FY27 call (July 2026), management stated that Net Interest Margin (NIM) would see "some pressure in Q2" before recovering in Q3 and Q4, while aiming to grow in line with the market for the year. For Q2 FY27, Net Interest Income grew 3.6% YoY to ₹4,569.4 crore.

evidence.quote: We've already seen NIM drop a bit in the first quarter. We'll have some pressure in Q2, start going back Q3, Q4
I think our broad, if I may use the word guidance, has been that we will grow in line with market this year with an exit ROA of 1%, and we stand by that
